title: Plenum prefetch: chaotic-mitigation and attention-ahead scheduler
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce tail latency and jitter from irregular microbursts by combining an admission gate that smooths chaotic arrival patterns with an attention-ahead scheduler that prefetches KV slices and biases kernel selection for likely decode paths.
background: We still see 99th/99.9th token-latency spikes for multi-tenant workloads that exhibit bursty prefill patterns (short prefill followed by long decodes) and mis-matched kernel choices when sequence length distribution changes mid-batch. Existing admission controllers apply coarse rate smoothing and the kernel selector reacts only after token shapes are known, which causes kernel warmup penalties and KV cache misses that inflate tails.
proposal: Implement a two-part runtime change: (1) Plenum admission gate - a lightweight burst model that maintains a short-term token budget per tenant and probabilistically defers or staggers prefill admission in tight bursts to avoid micro-congestion; and (2) Attention-Ahead Scheduler - a prediction-driven prefetcher that inspects prefill tokens and early decode tokens to warm KV cache slices and favor low-latency kernels (float16/quantized) for expected sequence lengths. The admission gate uses a tunable token-smoothing window and a tiny credit bucket per route; the scheduler emits speculative prefetch requests to the kernel layer and surfaces kernel affinity hints to the kernel selection API.
design_notes:
- Keep admission gate opt-in per route; default off for high-priority customers.
- Prediction model: simple heuristic ensemble (first-8-token length heuristics + recent route length histogram) to avoid heavy ML infra.
- Kernel affinity: annotate requests with preferred execution path and fallback path. Kernels must be able to accept warmup hints without changing correctness.
- Prefetch semantics: prefetch only KV ranges required for the predicted attention windows; avoid fetching full-value for very long context to protect memory.
- Ensure metrics for credit exhaustions, prefetched hit-rate, kernel-affinity-follow-rate, and tail-latency per-tenant are emitted.
success_metrics: reduce 99.9th token latency by >=20% on noisy tenants
reduce number of tail incidents attributed to kernel mis-selection by >=30%
prefetch hit rate >=70% on sampled workloads
admission-induced requeue rate < 0.5% for non-bursty routes
tasks: prototype plenum admission gate in runtime edge loop
add token-credit accounting and per-route opt-in flag
implement attention-ahead heuristic and KV prefetch API
extend kernel-selector to accept affinity hints and a warmup path
add observability: per-tenant tail traces and prefetch diagnostics
integration test: synthetic microburst harness + 5 benchmark scenarios
rollout canary and control-group telemetry collection
acceptance_criteria: canary shows 15-25% 99.9th latency improvement on bursty synthetic traces
no regression in median latency across baseline workloads
kernel-selector accepts hints and falls back correctly in failure cases
prefetch diagnostics show safely bounded memory usage (< 5% overhead) and hit-rate >= 70% in canary
risks_and_mitigations: prediction misfires could increase work: mitigate by conservative prefetch (prefetch only top-n ranges) and immediate cancellation hooks
admission gating could add latency for high-priority routes: mitigate with per-route override and SLO tags
kernel affinity hints may conflict with existing autoscaler placement: add affinity as advisory and ensure selector still measures real-time performance before committing long-running kernel choice
rollout_plan: deploy admission gate and scheduler to canary cluster (10% traffic) for 1 week
analyze telemetry and compare canary vs control using bench dashboards
increase to 50% for 3 days, run automated failback test
full rollout with per-customer opt-out window
